core_obligations: Choose the set of all closed points of degree at most N and let Gamma be the normal closed subgroup generated by their Frobenius elements (proof lines 4164-4171). If Gamma were proper, a proper normal open subgroup U containing it exists, corresponding to a finite etale Galois cover Y -> X with group G = pi_1(X)/U (proof lines 4172-4181). The Riemann hypothesis for X supplies chosen points of degrees N and N-1, so the degree map on Gamma and hence on U is surjective and Y_kbar is irreducible (proof lines 4173-4181). All points of degree at most N split completely in Y, so #Y(k_N) >= #G #X(k_N) (proof lines 4183-4186). Applying the Riemann hypothesis on both sides and Riemann-Hurwitz 2g_Y - 2 = #G(2g_X - 2) gives an inequality q^N + 1 + (#G)(2g_X - 1) q^{N/2} >= #G (q^N + 1 - 2g_X q^{N/2}) (proof lines 4186-4197), which fails for nontrivial G when N is large. Hence G is trivial, U = pi_1(X), and Gamma = pi_1(X) (proof lines 4198-4200).
proof_roadmap: Assume the generated subgroup is proper and build the corresponding Galois cover (proof lines 4164-4181).
Count points of bounded degree that split completely and derive the contradiction from the Riemann hypothesis bounds (proof lines 4183-4200).
